newsitem.title: USA: Sears, Roebuck posts record earnings.
newsitem.headline: Sears, Roebuck posts record earnings.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. posted record earnings for the third quarter Wednesday, fuelled by hefty apparel demand and strong gains at its credit card unit despite rising delinquencies in consumer debt.

Sears, the nation's third-largest retailer, said earnings jumped 22 percent to $279 million, or 68 cents a share, in the third quarter, compared with profits of $228 million, or 56 cents a share, a year ago.
The results, which were the seventh straight quarter of record earnings for Sears, beat Wall Street's estimates for income of 64 cents a share.

"Customers have responded enthusiastically to our department store renovations, broader assortments and quality brands, especially in apparel, and are heavily shopping our off-the-mall stores," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Arthur C. Martinez.
"Our excellent revenue growth, improved domestic gross margins and strong credit business led to record third-quarter earnings," he said.
The robust results caused Wall Street analysts to lift their estimates for Sears' full-year earnings. The company's shares rose $2 to $50.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"They clearly have been gaining market share all year," said Thomas Tashjian of Montgomery Securities. "I think they'll have a good fourth quarter."
Sears is feeling the benefits of a 1993 restructuring in which it closed its famed catalogue and chopped 50,000 jobs.
By the end of this year, it will have remodeled 450 of its 800 department stores and added about four million square feet of selling space by stripping back-office space in its stores.
During the third quarter, the company's credit card operation posted robust earnings despite more damage from personal bankruptcies and overdue bills among consumers.
For the second quarter in a row, Sears boosted its reserve to cover costs of uncollectible credit card accounts, raising it by 53 percent in the third quarter to $286 million.

"This is occurring at a point where the employment picture is the best it's been in several years," said David Levy, director of forecasting for the Jerome Levy Economics Institute in Mt. Kisco, N.Y. "The stores that still do give a lot of store credit have to view themselves as vulnerable."
He noted that consumer debt accounts for about 84 cents of every dollar of personal income, and the cost of paying for that credit also has grown, jumping nearly to its 1989 peak.

Sears has taken steps to combat the rising costs of bad debt, and the tide of delinquencies seems to have peaked, Wall Street analysts said. Last year, the retailer introduced uniform interest costs, which hiked rates for consumers in certain states. It also increased costs for late payments.
Sears' credit card revenue jumped by 19 percent, and analysts estimate income rose by double digits during the quarter. Sears does not break out income for the business.
"It doesn't worry me," said Montgomery Securities' Tashjian said of the increase in Sears' reserve for bad debt. "This is what you go through cyclically in the economy."

In retailing, Sears' same-store sales, or sales at stores open a year, have risen by more than 6 percent this year, more than its department store competitors. Sears has attempted to improve sales by stocking more attractive apparel and more appealing brands.
While apparel sales were strong, price competition hurt Sears' margins on hardgoods, including appliances and electronics, analysts said.

The company said its operations in Canada and Mexico lost $13 million, compared with a loss of $7 million in the third quarter of 1995. Sears Canada had a third-quarter pre-tax charge of $17 million from a previously announced restructuring plan.
